title: Three levels: affective, perceptual and cognitive consciousness

statements.text: Consciousness comes in three levels: arousal itself, called affective consciousness, the arousal of representations by attention, called perceptual consciousness, and the reflective re-representation of both, called cognitive consciousness. Following Tulving they correspond to anoetic, noetic and autonoetic consciousness, and roughly to the upper brainstem, the subcortical ganglia and upper limbic structures, and the neocortex.

sources.quote: This suggests a three-level taxonomy of consciousness
This kind of a conceptual scheme can be readily overlaid on some major evolutionary passages of the brain
